nudges.title: Start the paper chain
nudges.body: Add one link to the paper chain: a small good thing from your year, in a few words. Finished a tricky job, learned a new system, kept a houseplant alive. Watch the chain grow across the masthead all month. On door 23 we print the whole thing, with no names attached.

nudges.title: The Great Desk Debate
nudges.body: How many mince pies a day is correct?
options: I’ve lost count and I’m at peace with it

nudges.title: Pull a cracker
nudges.body: Pick a colleague and pull a Christmas cracker with them. They’ll find the hat, the prize and a dreadful joke in their pigeonhole. It takes one tap and costs nothing but your dignity.

nudges.title: Another cracker?
nudges.body: The cracker supply has been replenished. Pick a colleague who could do with a paper hat today.

nudges.title: Hand out a gold star
nudges.body: Give a colleague a gold star. Choose a reason and, if you like, add a few words of your own. It lands quietly in their pigeonhole.

nudges.title: No button today
nudges.body: Think of someone who’s had a heavy month. Send them a message today, anywhere but here: a quick “thinking of you”, a meme, a thank-you. Nobody will know whether you did it. That’s rather the point.

nudges.title: Paper hat Friday
nudges.body: Wear a paper hat on a call today. A cracker hat, a newspaper hat or one folded from a work document all count. Then press the button and your name joins the hat parade below.

nudges.title: The Great Desk Debate
nudges.body: What’s the ideal temperature for Christmas Day?

nudges.title: More gold stars
nudges.body: The gold star cupboard has been restocked. Who’s earned one this month?

nudges.title: The last crackers
nudges.body: The final crackers of the year. Pull one with someone you haven’t pulled one with yet.

nudges.title: The Great Desk Debate
nudges.body: When should Christmas decorations go up?

cracker_prizes: a paper hat in a colour that suits nobody
a tiny screwdriver for a screw that doesn’t exist
a plastic ring that fits no finger
a miniature pack of cards, missing the seven of clubs
cracker_jokes: Why was the Christmas tree bad at meetings?
It kept getting needled.
What’s a tree surgeon’s favourite carol?
Oak Come, All Ye Faithful.
Where do biscuit tins go on holiday?
Tin-erife.
Why did the biscuit go to the doctor?
It was feeling crummy.
What’s a tree’s favourite day of the working week?
Fir-day.
What did one Christmas light say to the other?
Let’s not get too wired.
Why did the email go to the Christmas party?
It was forwarded an invitation.
How does a sheep say Merry Christmas?
Fleece Navidad.
What did the stamp say to the Christmas card?
Stick with me and we’ll go places.
Why are Christmas trees terrible at knitting?
They keep dropping their needles.
What do you call Santa when he stops for a break?
Santa Pause.
What do you call a reindeer with no eyes?
No idea.
What do elves learn at school?
The elf-abet.
What’s the best thing to put in a Christmas pudding?
Your spoon.
Why did the arborist bring a ladder to the party?
He heard the drinks were on the top shelf.
What do you call a snowman in Sydney in December?
A puddle.
